title: Steering Without Side Effects: Improving Post-Deployment Control of Language Models
measurement_description: The paper lists 'Religion Bias' as one of 14 categories used to create a custom jailbreak robustness benchmark. The authors generated 20-40 plain requests for this category to evaluate whether language models would exhibit toxic or biased behavior, though the religion category was excluded from the computationally intensive jailbreak-augmented subset of the testing.
findings: The paper does not report specific findings isolated to religion. 'Religion Bias' was used merely as one topic category within a broader adversarial robustness dataset to measure the overall toxicity and jailbreak success rate of models before and after applying their KL-then-steer (KTS) mitigation method.
